properties.name: Hardknott Pass eastern approach
properties.reason: Very steep, narrow mountain-pass approach with hairpins. Penfold can physically fit much of it, but the combination of gradient, bends and meeting traffic makes it an avoid-by-default route.

properties.name: Wrynose Pass eastern approach
properties.reason: Single-track mountain road with steep gradients and tight bends; suitable only as a deliberate scenic route in Penfold.

properties.name: Red Bank Road Grasmere–Langdale
properties.reason: Single-track road with very tight corners; National Park guidance warns it is unsuitable for caravans and lorries. Penfold is smaller, but it remains a deliberate-route road.

properties.name: Honister Pass
properties.reason: Steep, narrow and twisty pass. Penfold-sized vans can use it, but gradients and encounters with oncoming traffic require care.

properties.name: Newlands Pass
properties.reason: Narrow mountain road with steep sections and limited passing. Better treated as an intentional scenic route than a sat-nav shortcut.

properties.name: Whinlatter Pass B5292
properties.reason: Proper through-road but steep and bendy. Generally suitable for Penfold with normal mountain-road care.

properties.name: A592 Kirkstone Pass
properties.reason: Main mountain A-road and normally suitable for Penfold, but steep gradients, bends and winter conditions justify care.

properties.name: A591 Ambleside–Keswick
properties.reason: Principal Lake District route, routinely used by coaches and larger vehicles. Preferred Penfold corridor over minor-road alternatives.

properties.name: Bwlch y Groes
properties.reason: High, steep and narrow mountain crossing with tight bends. Penfold can fit, but this should be chosen deliberately rather than used as a routine through-route.

properties.name: Gospel Pass
properties.reason: Very narrow high-level road with constrained passing and seasonal visitor pressure. Penfold-sized, but reversing and meeting traffic can be difficult.

properties.name: A4069 Black Mountain Pass
properties.reason: Twisty mountain A-road with exposed sections but no inherent Penfold dimensional problem. Suitable with sensible speed and weather awareness.

properties.name: A4086 Llanberis Pass
properties.reason: Penfold fits, but rock faces, buses, parking pressure and tourist traffic can create tight encounters.

properties.name: A5 Betws-y-Coed–Llangollen corridor
properties.reason: Major strategic route and the sensible Penfold alternative to many narrow mountain crossings.

properties.name: A487 Pembrokeshire trunk corridor
properties.reason: Main coastal trunk route and generally the best Penfold through-route compared with minor coastal lanes.

properties.name: Bealach na Bà
properties.reason: Famous single-track alpine-style pass with hairpins and steep gradients. Penfold is around the scale of campervan that can use it, but it is not a casual route and conditions/traffic matter.

properties.name: B869 Drumbeg coastal road
properties.reason: Narrow, twisting single-track coastal road. Larger motorhomes are commonly directed to alternatives; Penfold is smaller but still needs deliberate passing-place driving.

properties.name: A894 Kylesku–Scourie
properties.reason: Main-road alternative to the tighter Drumbeg coastal route and a straightforward Penfold corridor.

properties.name: A838 Durness–Tongue
properties.reason: Remote Highland route with significant single-track sections. Penfold is a suitable scale, but passing-place etiquette and weather matter.

properties.name: A832 Gairloch coastal corridor
properties.reason: Scenic Highland A-road with narrower/single-track stretches. Generally a good Penfold road, but slower than a normal A-road.

properties.name: A87 Skye trunk road
properties.reason: Primary Skye road used by coaches and commercial traffic; default green for Penfold.

properties.name: Quiraing road
properties.reason: Narrow single-track scenic road with steep sections and heavy visitor traffic. Penfold fits, but congestion and reversing make it a deliberate route.

properties.name: Neist Point road
properties.reason: Long single-track dead-end road with tourist traffic and limited passing. Suitable for Penfold but potentially slow and awkward at busy times.

properties.name: A82 Fort William–Inverness
properties.reason: Major trunk route used by coaches and HGVs. Default green for Penfold unless temporary closures or weather intervene.

properties.name: A9 Perth–Inverness
properties.reason: Major strategic trunk road; straightforward Penfold route subject to normal incidents/weather.

properties.name: Winnats Pass
properties.reason: Steep, narrow limestone gorge road with tight bends and tourist traffic. Penfold can use it, but it is not a low-stress through-route.

properties.name: Snake Pass A57
properties.reason: Bendy and exposed but a normal A-road. Penfold suitability is good; closures and weather are the bigger risks.

properties.name: A628 Woodhead Pass
properties.reason: Strategic trans-Pennine route carrying substantial commercial traffic; default green for Penfold.

properties.name: Buttertubs Pass
properties.reason: Narrow exposed moorland road with steep sections and limited passing. Penfold can use it, but it deserves deliberate-route status.

properties.name: Fleet Moss road
properties.reason: High, narrow and exposed single-track route with steep approaches. Meeting traffic and weather are the main Penfold concerns.

properties.name: A684 Wensleydale
properties.reason: Main east-west Dales route and a sensible Penfold corridor compared with minor pass roads.

properties.name: A65 Skipton–Kendal
properties.reason: Major access route around the Dales and straightforward for Penfold.

properties.name: B3212 Dartmoor
properties.reason: Main moorland B-road, generally suitable for Penfold but with livestock, bends and tourist traffic. Prefer it over tiny sat-nav shortcuts.
properties.evidence: official Dartmoor motorhome guidance + mapped B-road

properties.name: Widecombe minor lanes
properties.reason: Dartmoor guidance warns that some local roads are too narrow for motorhomes. Minor lanes around Widecombe should be treated cautiously rather than as routine shortcuts.

properties.name: Porlock Hill A39
properties.reason: Exceptionally steep main road but wide enough for normal vehicles. Penfold should use appropriate gears and engine braking; dimensional suitability itself is good.

properties.name: Lynton–Valley of Rocks road
properties.reason: Narrow scenic local road with constrained sections and visitor traffic. Check the exact approach rather than following a sat-nav blindly.

properties.name: B3306 St Ives–St Just
properties.reason: Spectacular but narrow and bendy coastal B-road. Penfold is an appropriate size; summer meeting traffic is the main difficulty.

properties.name: Mousehole village approach
properties.reason: Tight granite-walled approach and constrained village streets. Use signed visitor access and parking rather than centre-bound sat-nav routes.

properties.name: Port Isaac village approach
properties.reason: Very tight historic-village roads. Use designated visitor parking and avoid driving toward the old centre.

properties.name: A30 Cornwall
properties.reason: Primary strategic route through Cornwall and strongly preferable to hedge-bound sat-nav shortcuts.
